functions.name: call
functions.desc:
Call any function by name, as the same caller. `args` is positional (an array) or named (an
object); leaving it out calls the function with no arguments. A list of `{name, args}` is a
batch: called in order with nothing else running in between, answering every result; it stops
at the first error, which names the call, and what earlier calls did is not undone.

items.description: One call of a batch: a function and its arguments.

examples.desc: Named arguments, as the CLI sends them.
A batch: two calls in one round trip.

functions.name: clipboard.get
functions.desc: The clipboard's text: `null` when it holds none.

functions.name: clipboard.set
functions.desc: Put text on the clipboard; `null` clears it.

functions.name: event.emit
functions.desc:
Fire an event to every channel subscribed: mostly a plugin's own (`owner.name.done`), with
which plugins and scripts tell each other things, and the events channels have of their own
(the CLI's `plugin.reloadRequested`).

match.description: The event's `match`: what its listeners' `match` is tested against.

tab.description: The tab it is about; one just closed may be named.

functions.name: event.off
functions.desc: End a subscription (`event.on`'s handle); whether there was one.

functions.name: event.on
functions.desc:
Subscribe to events, by name or glob (`tab.*`; `*` is every event but those fired before
what they name, in `-ing`). Each one that fires goes to the caller's channel
as `{"method": "rpc.event", "params": [subscription, event]}`, until `event.off` or the
channel closes. Answers the subscription's integer handle.

event.description: The events `event.on` and `event.wait` hear: one name, or a list of at least one.

anyOf.description: One name or several.

match.description:
Globs matched against the event's `match` (a tab's id for `tab.changed`, a request's
kind for `request.opened`); every match without one.

once.description: End the subscription after its first event.

desc.description: What it is for, as a listing shows it.

functions.name: event.wait
functions.desc:
Wait for an event, by name or glob: the call answers when one that matches fires, with the
event (`{event, match, session, view, tab, data}`), or with `null` when `timeout` passes or
the caller goes. A wait that times out is not an error.

event.description: The events `event.on` and `event.wait` hear: one name, or a list of at least one.

anyOf.description: One name or several.

match.description:
Globs matched against the event's `match` (a tab's id for `tab.changed`, a request's id
for `request.closed`); any match without one.

timeout.description: Seconds to wait; none: until it fires.

anyOf.description: What `event.wait` waits for, beside the event's name.
An event as `event.wait` answers it.

examples.desc: The next change to tab 3, for ten seconds.
Until request 7 is answered or closed.

notes: In `call.atomic` it does not wait: it answers `null`.

functions.name: fn.set
functions.desc:
Provide a function every surface can call (`pumi call git.status`, a script's
`pumi.api["git.status"]`): calls to it from any channel come to this one as requests, with
the caller in `rpc.caller`, and its answers go back; or, for one with a `callback`, as a
`rpc.callback` notification, while the call answers `null`. It appears in `api.getInfo` with
the rest. A core function cannot be provided, and nor can one another channel provides as
someone else (another plugin, another program): it is theirs until they withdraw it. With
`runsOn: "client"` each app provides its own, for its own client. `null` withdraws it; it goes
with the channel too.

anyOf.description: What a provided function does: a read, or a write (the default).

paramsSchema.description: A JSON Schema for its arguments; one that takes any object without it.

returnsSchema.description: A JSON Schema for its answer.

callback.description:
Send each call here as a `rpc.callback` notification, with its arguments in order, and
answer `null`: `{"chan": 0, "ref": …}`, a reference a channel holds. Without one the
call comes to the channel as a request, and its answer is the call's.

anyOf.description: Where a provided function runs: for everyone (`server`), or in each client's own app.

runsOn.description:
`client`: each app that provides it answers the calls made for its own client (its
clipboard, its updater), and others' go to the first app that does. `server` by default:
one channel answers every call.

anyOf.description: A function `fn.set` provides: what it does, its arguments and its answer.

examples.desc: A function run by a callback; the call answers `null`.

functions.name: fs.list
functions.desc:
The entries of a folder on the server's machine: `~` and `~/…` are its home, a relative path
is in it, and an empty path is the home itself. Hidden entries are left out unless `hidden`,
and `recursive` lists every folder under it too; both sorted by name, case-insensitively.

recursive.description: Every folder under it, not only its own entries.

kind.description: What a path in a listing is.

functions.name: fs.open
functions.desc:
Open a path in its default app, or in the one `with` names; `reveal` shows it in the file
manager instead.

reveal.description: Show it in the file manager (the Finder, Explorer) instead of opening it.

with.description: The app to open it with: by name on macOS (`Safari`), a program elsewhere (`code`).

functions.name: fs.pick
functions.desc:
Choose files to open, or a folder: a native picker. Answers the path chosen, the paths when
it takes more than one, and `null` when it was cancelled.

oneOf.description: Files to open.
A folder.

multiple.description: Allow choosing more than one file.

title.description: What the picker's button says (`Open Local Folder`).

path.description:
Where it starts: a file's folder, or a folder. Taken but not followed: the system's
picker opens where it last was.

functions.name: fs.trash
functions.desc: Move paths to the Trash.

functions.name: menu.set
functions.desc:
Set a menu item: `path` names it and every menu above it, which are made as needed, and the
item is the function choosing it calls, with its title and when it shows. Setting a path
again replaces the item; `null` removes it, and a menu with everything in it.

args.description: Its arguments, positional or by name; none by default.

title.description: What it says in the menu; made of the function's name by default.

when.description: When it shows; always without it.

anyOf.description: A menu item as `menu.set` takes it.

functions.name: option.get
functions.desc:
An option's value in a scope: the object's own, else the one it inherits, else the default.
A plugin's is its own store, and a `secret` one is in the OS keychain.

scope.description:
`global`, `session`, `view`, `tab` or `plugin`. Without it: the option's own scope, at the
object `id` names (the caller's own without that).

oneOf.description: One plugin's own store (`plugin` names it).

plugin.description: The plugin whose store it is, for `{scope: "plugin"}`: `owner/name`.

functions.name: option.set
functions.desc:
Set an option on an object, in a plugin's store, or globally. `@name` options need no
declaration. Setting a type's option is acting on the tab: a browser's `url` navigates.
`null` unsets it, so it inherits again. `ttl` makes the value expire, and a report whose `seq`
is not past the last one from the same `source` is dropped.

oneOf.description: One plugin's own store (`plugin` names it).

scope.description: Which object an option is read from or set on, by scope.

ttl.description: Seconds the value holds for; then it is the one it inherits again.

source.description: Who set it (`report-agent`'s reporter); the caller's source by default.

seq.description: With `source`: a report older than the last one from it is dropped.

functions.name: pane.close
functions.desc: Close a pane and every tab in it. No id is the caller's tab's pane.

functions.name: pane.focus
functions.desc:
Give a pane its view's focus (its front tab becomes the view's active tab), and make its view
and session current; or move from it to another: the one beside it (`direction`), so many
on (`offset`), or the one used last (`last`). No id is the caller's tab's pane. Moving out of
a zoomed pane unzooms the view; nothing there is not an error.

anyOf.description: Where a new pane goes beside an existing one.

direction.description: To the pane beside it on this side.

offset.description: To so many panes on (or back, negative), in layout order, wrapping.

last.description: To the pane of its view's tab used last.

anyOf.description: Where `pane.focus` moves from its pane.

examples.desc: The pane left of the caller's.
The next pane, in layout order.

functions.name: pane.get
functions.desc:
A pane: its view, its tabs in its strip's order, the one in front, and whether it has the
focus or is zoomed. No id is the caller's tab's pane.

tabs.description: Its tabs, in the order its strip shows them.

returns_schema.description: A pane, as `pane.get` answers it: an area of a view's layout and the tabs it holds.

functions.name: pane.list
functions.desc: List panes: a view's, or every view's, in layout order.

anyOf.description: Which panes `pane.list` lists.

functions.name: pane.update
functions.desc: Zoom a pane, or move its borders. No id is the caller's tab's pane.

anyOf.description: The word that says to flip a view's zoom.
`tab.update`'s `zoom`: zoom or unzoom, or flip it.

zoom.description:
Fill its view with it, its tab strip on top (`true`), give the view its layout back
(`false`), or flip it (`"toggle"`).

anyOf.description: Cells to move a pane's borders by, a side at a time.

resize.description: Grow (or, negative, shrink) it by so many cells from each side given.

examples.desc: Five cells wider, to the right.

functions.name: plugin.add
functions.desc:
Install a plugin: a store id (`owner/name`, or a name only one listing has), a GitHub
repository (`owner/repo`, or `owner/repo/dir` for one in a folder), a git URL, or a directory
on this machine, which is linked. The commit installed is recorded; a manifest's `minPumi`
newer than this pumi is refused. One from git with `dependencies` has them installed (`bun
install --production --no-save --ignore-scripts`), and is refused when they fail to install.
An install from GitHub is counted by the store
(`pluginindex`'s server, once per address a day). One already installed stays as it is.
Answers its id (`owner/name`).

version.description: The git ref to follow: a tag, a branch, a commit.

linked.description: Link a directory on this machine instead of copying it.

enabled.description: Start it once installed (`true`, the default); `false` installs it turned off.

functions.name: plugin.contribute
functions.desc:
Change what a running plugin contributes, without starting it again: `patch` is a JSON merge
patch (RFC 7396) over its `contributes` as they are now (an object merges into an object, `null`
takes a key away, anything else replaces what was there, a list as a whole), checked as its
manifest is. Settings, the palette, keys, blocks and the window's slots follow at once. `null`
gives back what its manifest says, as the plugin stopping does; nothing is written to it.

functions.name: plugin.remove
functions.desc:
Uninstall a plugin. A linked one's directory stays: only the link goes. What it kept stays
too, unless `data` says.

data.description:
Also what it kept: its own `config`, `state` and `cache` directories
(`stdpath(…)/plugins/<owner.name>`, its options' store among them), and its `secret`
options in the keychain. Without it they stay, for when it is installed again.

functions.name: plugin.update
functions.desc:
Patch a plugin, or refresh it from its source: a linked one is read again where it is, and a
git one is fetched and checked out at the ref it follows (or the one `version` gives), and its
dependencies are installed when they changed or are missing. What
its manifest contributes is read again, and the app starts it again. `enabled` turns it on or
off, and it stays installed.

enabled.description: Turn it on or off; it stays installed.

version.description: Follow another git ref from now on (a tag, a branch, a commit).

patch.description: How `plugin.update` patches one, or refreshes it from its source.

functions.name: process.list
functions.desc:
The processes on this machine, matching the fields given: `pid`, `command` (any part of its
command line), and `cwd` (its directory). No fields matches every process.

command.description: The processes whose command line contains this.

cwd.description: The processes whose directory is this one.

cpu.description: How much processor it uses: percent of one core, over its whole life (as `ps` reports it).

cwd.description:
`null` unless a `cwd` was asked for (reading it takes a system call a process), and on
Windows.

items.description:
One process: its id, its parent's, its processor and memory use, its command line as its
arguments, and its directory (when it is known).

examples.desc: One process; empty when there is none
The ones running in a directory

functions.name: registry.list
functions.desc:
Registered entries of one kind: functions, blocks, traits and options; the key bindings; the
menus; the plugins (or the store's, with `available`); the themes; the viewers of a file
(`path`); the methods `tab.call` answers; the models; and the plugins' pages and sections in
Settings. `{name}` picks one entry.

oneOf.description: Every function, core and provided.
What a tab holds.
What a tab is beside its block.
A declared option.
A key binding.
A menu item.
An installed plugin, or with `available` one in the store.
A colour scheme a plugin brings.
A plugin that can draw a file, for a `path`.
What `tab.call` answers: a method, its arguments and the blocks that answer it.
What a `get` answers: a model and its fields.
A plugin's page or section in Settings (`contributes.settings`).

kind.description: The kinds `registry.list` lists, in the order the export names them.

name.description:
One entry by its name (a function's, a block's, a trait's, an option's, a menu's path, a
tab method's; a model's, in any case).

available.description: `plugin`: search the store's listings for `name` instead of the installed ones.

path.description: `viewer`: the file the viewer is for.

palette.description: `fn`: the palette's entries, with the title a manifest's command gives them.

functions.name: request.close
functions.desc:
Close a request: answer it, or dismiss it without `answer`. A notification takes no answer.
The first close wins: a request already closed is not found.

answer.description:
Its answer: `{"option": id}` picks one of its options, `{"text": …}` answers a question in
words (other fields go along). Without, it is closed unanswered.

functions.name: request.get
functions.desc: An open request.

oneOf.description: Something to know; it takes no answer.
May an agent do something (run a tool)?
Something asked of the user.

kind.description: What a request puts to the user.

oneOf.description: Only kept: never posted to the OS.

anyOf.description: How much a request matters.

group.description: A notification opened with the group of one still open replaces it.

anyOf.description: How urgent a notification is to the OS.

data.description: Carried back with what the user does with it.

anyOf.description: What a notification does in the OS's notification centre.

source.description: Who opened it: a plugin's id, or its channel's name.

expires.description: RFC 3339; `null`: it stays until it is closed.

returns_schema.description:
An open request, as `request.get` answers it and `request.opened` carries it (with `id`
spelled `request`).

functions.name: request.list
functions.desc: The open requests, oldest first: every one, or those of `tab` and of `kind`.

oneOf.description: Something to know; it takes no answer.
May an agent do something (run a tool)?
Something asked of the user.

anyOf.description: What a request puts to the user.

functions.name: request.open
functions.desc:
Put something to the user: a notification (`kind: "notification"`, no `options`), a
permission for what runs in `tab` (the `tool` and the `options` to allow or reject it), or a
question. Whoever listens to `request.opened` shows it, and anyone may answer it with
`request.close(id, {answer})`; the first answer wins, and `request.closed` says how it ended.
pumi-host posts notifications to the OS's notification centre and takes them back when they
close. Answers the request's id.

oneOf.description: Something to know; it takes no answer.
May an agent do something (run a tool)?
Something asked of the user.

kind.description: What a request puts to the user.

title.description: One line: what is asked or said (`Run "rm -rf build"?`).

tool.description: The tool a permission is for (`Bash`).

options.description:
The answers it offers: a permission's are `{id, label, kind}`; a question may offer none
and take text; a notification has none.

oneOf.description: Only kept: never posted to the OS.

anyOf.description: How much a request matters.

group.description: A notification opened with the group of one still open replaces it.

anyOf.description: How urgent a notification is to the OS.

data.description: Carried back with what the user does with it.

anyOf.description: What a notification does in the OS's notification centre.

request.description: What `request.open` is asked to put to the user.

tab.description: The tab it is for; a permission has one.

expires.description:
When it closes unanswered (`timeout`), RFC 3339. A permission or a question expires in
300 seconds without; a notification stays until it is closed.

source.description: Who opens it; the caller's plugin, or its channel's name, without.

examples.desc: Ask whether what runs in tab 3 may deploy; wait for `request.closed` with `match: "+8"`.
One with the same `group` open is replaced.

notes: A permission or a question opened while nothing listens to `request.opened` is refused (`provider_unavailable`): nobody would see it.
A permission or a question is cancelled when the channel that opened it closes.
At most 256 notifications are open at once; past that, the oldest is closed.

functions.desc:
Change a session's name or directory. Fires `session.changed` with what changed. No id is the
caller's session.

functions.name: tab.call
functions.desc:
Call a method of the block in a tab: the protocol every block answers (`read`, its text;
`input`, `{text}`, `{paste}` or `{keys}`; `selection`; `report`, an OSC 7501 body), a
terminal's `run`, `wait` and `attach`, and the block's own methods — a terminal's `respawn`, a
plugin block's `<block>.<method>`, a file tab's `<viewer>.<method>`. `tab` is the caller's own
when it is `null`.

or move from it: to the next tab of its pane (`offset`), to the pane beside it (`direction`),

functions.name: tab.open
functions.desc:
Open a tab holding `block`, placed as `place` says: in a pane split from a tab's, into a pane
as one of its tabs (`{"pane": ":2"}`), in a new view or session, floating; or in an open tab
instead of its block (`{"kind": "tiled", "replace": "%1"}`), which
keeps its id, place, focus and options (`tab.changed {block}`). It is the one way anything
appears. `args` are the block's (a terminal's `command`, `cwd` and `env`; a file's `path`; a
page's `url`), or `{"state": …}` to restore a saved state into the tab. Returns the tab's id.

notes: Without a place, the tab is tiled in a pane below the caller's tab's.

A float's `width` and `height` are cells, `"480px"` or a share of what it floats over (`"50%"`, the default), kept as given so a share stays one as the window changes size.
A float is pinned by `anchor` (`NW` … `SE`, `center`), `row` and `col` in from it; without an anchor it is centred on each axis it was given no offset for.
